summary: Implemented, locally only (HD-0015), a trusted-base verification tool (ops/lib/trusted-base.mjs) that judges a change with the validator, policy and schemas of an established base revision, reading the head only as data and never executing it, and a CI evidence document (ops/lib/ci-evidence.mjs, ops/ci-evidence.mjs, a strict schema registered in the validator) built from GitHub's Actions and Checks data with expectations taken from the base, test counts labelled as claims and the first live run (43995081483) stored as a fixture. A second job in ci.yml was deliberately NOT added: it would not be an independent boundary, so the result is always advisory_only, nothing is claimed as independent enforcement, and control-plane changes stay human-approved (ADR-0012, TRUSTED_CI.md). 64 new negative-heavy tests on real throwaway git repositories; a 30-weakening mutation check found four untested rules, now tested. Documented the evidence design, exact GitHub branch rules for main and claude-dev with what is observable (and the finding that Claude acts as the owner, so rules bind it only as far as they bind the owner), the eight Reel commits, and the next task (OPS-0004 proposal). Updated project memory to the verified reality: HD-0014 (one-time push and first live run), HD-0015, OQ-0035, OQ-0036, REC-OPS-022..024. Nothing is pushed; nothing ran on GitHub for this branch.

unresolved_issues.description: Nothing in OPS-0003 has run on GitHub. The tool and the evidence format were tested only on fixtures and throwaway repositories. A first run needs a push, which needs the owner's explicit approval naming the branch (OQ-0028).

The trusted-base check is advisory. It becomes independent only when it is run by something the change cannot alter (the reviewer's trusted workspace, a required reviewer who is not the author, or an organisation-level required workflow). Until the owner chooses (OQ-0035), control-plane changes rely on human review.

Claude acts as the owner (the actor of every push and of run 43995081483), so branch rules bind the automation only as far as they bind the owner, and requiring approvals would block every merge unless the owner may bypass. A separate Write-only identity is the real hardening; whether a Claude session can use one is unverified (OQ-0036). No GitHub setting was observed beyond branch protection flags (all false) and collaborators (only the owner); rulesets, Actions settings and secrets are not observable from here.

The check-runs fixture is synthetic in shape (the app slug github-actions was not observed), and whether an unauthenticated client may download a job log from a public repository was not verified. The job log is optional in the evidence tool.

The evidence document is unauthenticated tool output. A consumer must fetch the GitHub data and run the tool itself from the base; signing would need a secret or an attestation action, neither approved.

The eight Reel commits and the creative file-mode change are untouched. Their path set is disjoint from this branch's, so they cannot conflict. Before any rule requiring pull requests is enabled on claude-dev, the owner should preserve them (bundle file or one named push to a separate branch), see GITHUB_SETTINGS_GUIDE.md section 7 and OQ-0019.

OQ-0035: which anchor do you accept for the trusted-base check: the reviewer's trusted workspace (recommended first), a required reviewer who is not the author, or an organisation-level required workflow?
OQ-0036: do you want to apply the single-identity branch rules now as safety rails (Profile 1), and investigate a separate Write-only identity for the automation before STG-6 (Profile 2)?
OQ-0034: do you set the Actions settings and the rulesets from GITHUB_SETTINGS_GUIDE.md, and confirm the settings I cannot observe (default token permission, fork-run approval)?
OQ-0019: how should the eight Reel commits be preserved and integrated (keep local with a bundle backup, one named push to a separate branch, or a separate private repository)?
